needs: dprod:deadline for the deletion window end
notes: The retention privilege translates directly. RL2's rl2:currentDateTime resolves to state.Clock, the snapshot evaluation time, so it is bound to dprod:clock (sotw.effective_at) — a context built-in, not a profile term — rather than odrl:dateTime, which DPROD would rebind anyway; xsd:dateTimeStamp becomes xsd:dateTime. The deletion duty is an independent clause, so it becomes a root odrl:obligation with the Customer as bearer through the policy-level assignee. It is in force for every request the retention permission matches, constraints aside (§5.2), so retain requests after expiry still report it. Its window start reads due2:actionTime, so it is a witness condition: deletion evidence before 2027-01-01 does not fulfil it. Its window end becomes an inclusive dprod:deadline at RL2's exclusive end, a one-instant difference accepted (due2-profiles.md §7). One status difference remains: before the window opens RL2 calls the duty Pending, while due2 has no not-yet-owed state for an obligation in force and reports it outstanding (scenario 1). RL2 states that the privilege is inapplicable from 2027-01-01 and that the duty's status follows the deletion evidence, but gives no decision for those snapshots, so scenarios 2–5 carry no rl2_expected. Scenarios 2–5 are added; scenario 5 is DPROD-faithful (violations = deny).

expected.why: dprod:clock = 2026-12-31T12:00Z < 2027-01-01, so ex:retentionUntil2027 applies with no duties. It matches the request, so ex:deleteAfterRetention is in force; no witness and its deadline has not passed, so it is outstanding (RL2: Pending, window not yet open). Under violations = ignore it does not affect the verdict.

scenarios.name: retain after expiry, not yet deleted

expected.why: dprod:clock < 2027-01-01 is F, so the permission does not apply; nothing prohibits. The permission still matches (constraints aside), so the obligation is in force: no witness, deadline 2027-01-02 not passed — outstanding (RL2: Active).

The permission is F on its clock constraint. The obligation is in force; ex:ev1 is a witness (actor ex:Customer, action, object, before effective_at and the deadline) and its action time 2027-01-01T10:00Z ≥ 2027-01-01, so it is fulfilled (RL2: Fulfilled).

ex:ev0 matches actor, action, and object, but its action time 2026-12-30 ≥ 2027-01-01 is F, so it fails the witness condition; every witness fails, so the obligation is outstanding. The permission is F.

The permission is F on its clock constraint but matches, so the obligation is in force; effective_at is past its deadline with no witness, so it is violated (RL2: Violated). Under violations = deny a violated obligation in force denies (§6.4); under the default ignore the verdict would be NotApplicable.
